page: Microsoft Azure E4as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Easv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The configuration includes 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10% tier. However, multi-core and multi-threaded scaling present a notable tradeoff. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average range, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is positioned in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 441.73 GB/sec and uncached large block write bandwidth at 33.69 GB/sec. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput also align with average tier expectations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4as_v7 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPU hardware, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-capacity local scratch space. Given its hardware profile and benchmark characteristics, this server is suited for relational database hosting, caching layers such as Redis, memory-intensive web serving, and lightweight data processing tasks. It is less suited for highly parallelized multi-threaded compute tasks or large-scale LLM inference, as demonstrated by its poor prompt processing speeds on 7B parameter models.
